## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

buildSegments — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/race/SegmentBuilder.kt

## Trigger

Already called wherever a Segment list is built from raw durations —
RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.markSegment (app-wear), RaceRepositoryImpl's
deriveSegments (core-data, on read), and ImportPreviewViewModel with the
parser's output (app-phone) — observed.

## Today

buildSegments takes a `List<Long?>` and turns each entry into a
`Segment` unchecked: a negative value passes through exactly as a
positive one would. Three sources can hand it a negative value —
HyresultResultParser.parseTimeValue splits a time value on `:` and
converts each component with `toLongOrNull()`, which accepts a leading
`-` and returns a negative diff with no rejection; markSegment in
RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl computes `durationMs = markedAtElapsedRealtime
- openedAt` and passes it straight into buildSegments with no check
that it is non-negative; RaceRepositoryImpl.deriveSegments (core-data)
re-reads whatever SegmentEntity.durationMs holds, itself an unbounded
`Long?` column, and passes it into buildSegments unchecked. Because
markSegment stores a negative duration as-is, undoLastMark in the same
class then does `restoredOpenedAt = openedAt - closedDurationMs` on
that already-negative value, which adds instead of subtracts and
further corrupts the reopened segment's start instant.

## Expected

buildSegments rejects a negative entry instead of turning it into a
Segment carrying it: a negative `durationMs` is treated the same way a
missing one already is — the resulting Segment carries `durationMs =
null` rather than the negative value. This one change reaches every
caller that already routes through buildSegments: HyresultResultParser's
negative diffs, markSegment's negative computed duration, and Room's
re-read of a corrupted stored value all come out as an absent duration,
displayed as a dash per §12 rather than a nonsensical negative time.
It also removes undoLastMark's compounding: `closedSegment.durationMs`
would be null for a segment buildSegments rejected, and undoLastMark
already returns the race unchanged when `closedDurationMs` is null —
so a segment that cannot carry a sensible duration is left alone by
undo rather than corrupted further.

PayloadCodec, in core-sync/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/sync/transport/PayloadCodec.kt,
is a second gap: its `SegmentSnapshot.toSegment()` builds a `Segment`
directly from the decoded `durationMs` field, bypassing buildSegments
entirely — both `decodeProfileSync` (reference and history) and
`decodeRecordedRace` reconstruct segments this way, out of the
bearer's reach. A negative value carried over the wire — from a
corrupted watch race being pushed to the phone, or a corrupted
reference pushed down to the watch — reaches the decoded Race
unchecked. `toSegment()` needs the same rejection buildSegments gets,
or to route through buildSegments itself.
